chapters.title: Chapter 1: Federal Appellate Jurisdiction and Interlocutory Review of Injunctions
chapters.description: Explains when and how federal courts of appeals may review preliminary injunctions and related orders before final judgment.
subtopics: Record on appeal in interlocutory review

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Stays Pending Appeal
chapters.description: Sets out the governing standards for granting a stay of a district court order while an appeal is pending and how courts balance equities.
subtopics: Four-factor test for stays pending appeal
Primacy of likelihood of success and irreparable harm
Comparing stays pending appeal with injunctions pending appeal

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Preliminary Injunctions and Temporary Restraining Orders
chapters.description: Covers the prerequisites for preliminary injunctive relief and the evidentiary and procedural framework in federal court.
subtopics: Public interest and balance of equities

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Standards of Review on Appeal of Preliminary Relief
chapters.description: Describes how appellate courts review preliminary injunctions and related equitable orders.
subtopics: De novo review of legal issues
Deference on national-security and foreign-affairs judgments

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Presidential Authority Over Entry of Aliens
chapters.description: Provides the statutory framework empowering the President to restrict the entry of noncitizens.
subtopics: Nature and form of proclamations and executive orders
Textual limits and duration of entry restrictions

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Refugee Law and the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program (USRAP)
chapters.description: Surveys the statutory and regulatory architecture governing refugee admissions to the United States.
subtopics: Annual admissions process and presidential determinations (8 U.S.C. § 1157)
Interagency roles: State Department, DHS, HHS/ORR
Numerical ceilings and consultations with Congress

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Refugee Resettlement Services and 8 U.S.C. § 1522
chapters.description: Details the domestic resettlement and assistance framework for refugees after admission.
subtopics: Office of Refugee Resettlement (HHS) roles and duties
Cash and medical assistance; support services
Statutory phrases: “shall,” “authorized,” and “to the extent of available appropriations”

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Administrative Procedure Act—Basics of Review
chapters.description: Introduces APA causes of action, thresholds for review, and standards governing agency decisionmaking.
subtopics: APA § 702 cause of action and waiver of sovereign immunity
Final agency action (Bennett v. Spear framework)
Remedies under the APA (vacatur, remand, injunctions)

chapters.title: Chapter 9: APA Review of Agency Implementation of Executive Orders
chapters.description: Explains how courts review agency actions taken to implement presidential directives while the President himself is not an APA ‘agency.’
subtopics: President excluded from APA (Franklin v. Massachusetts)
Challenging agency implementation rather than the EO itself
Administrative records in national security and foreign affairs contexts
Foreign affairs function exception to notice-and-comment (5 U.S.C. § 553(a)(1))
Justiciability limits where national security is invoked

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Federal Grants and Cooperative Agreements with Nonprofits
chapters.description: Covers the legal framework for federal assistance instruments used to deliver refugee services.
subtopics: Federal Grant and Cooperative Agreement Act (31 U.S.C. §§ 6301–6308)
Distinguishing procurement contracts from assistance instruments
Terms, conditions, and termination/suspension of cooperative agreements
Programmatic vs. contractual challenges (APA vs. contract remedies)
Reliance interests when altering or ending funded programs

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Federal Appropriations and Fiscal Law for Program Administration
chapters.description: Addresses how appropriations law constrains and enables agency program operations and funding decisions.
subtopics: “To the extent of available appropriations” clauses

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Statutory Interpretation of Authorization and Mandate Provisions
chapters.description: Equips readers with tools to parse whether a statute imposes duties or merely permits action, particularly in spending and program statutes.
subtopics: Weight of statutory titles and headings
Contextual reading within multi-part statutory schemes
Post-Chevron landscape: de novo review with Skidmore weight; major questions doctrine

chapters.title: Chapter 13: Standing and Justiciability in Immigration-Related Litigation
chapters.description: Outlines who may sue and what injuries suffice in cases challenging immigration and refugee policies.
subtopics: Article III injury, causation, and redressability
Statutory zone-of-interests under the INA and APA
Challenges by foreign nationals outside the U.S.
Ripeness and mootness in fast-moving policy disputes

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Scope and Tailoring of Equitable Relief Against the Federal Government
chapters.description: Discusses how courts shape remedies against federal agencies and officers, with sensitivity to separation-of-powers and nationwide effects.
subtopics: Public interest and comity in fashioning remedies
Limitations under the APA and equitable principles

chapters.title: Chapter 15: Separation of Powers and Conflicts Between Statutory Mandates and Executive Policy
chapters.description: Explores frameworks for evaluating executive action where congressional statutes set program baselines or duties.
subtopics: Delegations of authority vs. statutory constraints

chapters.title: Chapter 16: Landmark Cases—Nken v. Holder and the Law of Stays
chapters.description: Presents the key Supreme Court precedent establishing the modern test for stays pending appeal and its application.
subtopics: Nken’s four factors and their weighting
Practical guidance for stay motions and evidentiary showings

chapters.title: Chapter 17: Landmark Cases—Trump v. Hawaii, Mandel, and Deference in Entry Restrictions
chapters.description: Surveys the leading cases defining judicial deference to the political branches in regulating the entry of noncitizens.
subtopics: Kleindienst v. Mandel and the “facially legitimate and bona fide” standard
Interaction with Establishment Clause and equal protection arguments (overview)
Limits and open questions in deference doctrine
